findings.reason: the section must say the copy is written on first storage only, or that a re-queue leaves an existing `steering.md` alone, and add the arm "re-dispatch after an edit keeps the edited text", otherwise the one interaction §5 exists to guarantee is lost by the path §9 recommends.
findings.text: §5 says `_queued_request_record` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:229) "copies `--brief` into" `steering.md`, but that builder is called on three in-place re-queue paths as well as first storage: `_answer_existing_node_run` for a node that is already queued (dispatch.py:1733, whose own docstring says "A queued copy is updated in place"), the yielded-lane path (dispatch.py:1847), and the admission re-queue that stores a replaced request under a new id (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1583); `queue_dispatch` documents that "a repeat dispatch of a node the session already has queued only updates that pointer" (reckon/crew/runs.py:552-554), so a literal implementation of this sentence rewrites `steering.md` from the command's `--brief` every time the same node is dispatched again, discarding a `crew queue edit` — which §9 (line 84) then calls safe ("reloading a plan after an interruption is safe"), and no arm in §5's done-when exercises it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_queued_request_record` (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:229), `_node_from_pointer` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:119), `_launch_queued` (:171), `_store_brief` and `_brief_digest` (reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:2241, :2204), `RUN_DELIVERED_STATUSES` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:1023), `_readiness_rows` (:1056), `_priority_key` (reckon/roadmap_ranking.py:196), `STARVATION_AGE_SECONDS` (reckon/crew/queue_order.py:13) and `crew view live --phase` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:246) all resolve, as do the extensionless plan hrefs and `docs/evidence/archive/a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan-landed.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — each section names a negative or refusal arm; §5's discriminating arm (leave `steering.md` alone, change the brief on the queued pointer, digest must match `steering.md`) genuinely fails on today's code, which stores the pointer's brief text at launch.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — gate logs are declared under the run directory, and §14's record path `docs/evidence/archive/a-queue-holds-the-whole-plan-landed.html` exists in the repository.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §5 introduces `crew queue edit`, `reprioritise`, `drop`, `steering.md` and `awaiting-upstream`, none of which carries a plan label, stage name or ticket number, and its prose states mechanism rather than changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §5's root cause matches the code it cites (`_store_brief` copies the brief at dispatch, so a later edit of the source changes nothing the worker reads), and the caller of the launch-time read is named and real (`_launch_queued` is called from `admit_once` and from `dispatch()` at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:423), but the write site the section assigns to `_queued_request_record` also runs on in-place re-queue paths, where it would overwrite an edited `steering.md`.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each node names one deliverable; §5's two-node split (binding, then the verbs) is already recorded in followup f-aqhwp-002 and was declined earlier as one deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — every `plan-section-depends-on` ref in the snapshot resolves to an existing section of this plan, §3→§4 and §5→§2 are declared, and the cross-project wait on `imas-ambix:local-lane-admission-control#s27` is carried on §14.
